messages:
leah: quick summary from today's bench: vanguard-13b int6 vs int4, small slices (multi-turn summarization, entity-extraction, short QA). dropping numbers here.
omar: paste the table pls.
leah: results (short-run ~3k tok each):\\n\\n```\\nmodel                 | tps | p95(ms) | unit $/1k tok | QA delta vs int6\\nvanguard-13b-int6      | 98  | 240     | $0.95         | baseline\\nvanguard-13b-int4      | 170 | 330     | $0.53         | -2.6% overall; -4.4% long-summ\\n```\\n
leah: takeaways: int4 ~44% cost drop, big throughput win, but p95 hit and noticeable quality drift on long summarization and rare-entity recall. short QA & classification slices ~parity.
vik: how noisy are those deltas? any CI?
leah: bootstrap CI for overall QA delta ~0.8%. slice-level for long-summ ~1.6%. ran 4 seeds; direction consistent.
nina: product: customers using long-form summaries will notice. we need routing guidance.
omar: two deployment knobs: (1) default model for low-latency frontdoor flows; (2) a cost-optimized bucket for background/batch. propose mapping.
leah: suggested policy draft:
- default: keep int6 for frontdoor/GTN and tenant-default.
- batch/async: route to int4 by default for throughput jobs.
- hybrid: create "economy" route for opportunistic tasks (embeddings, backfills) -> int4.
- canary: shadow int4 at 3-5% for a week for multi-tenant traffic with summaries off.

vik: we should also try priming fixes and token-penalty tweaks; my past runs recovered ~1.2% on long-sum with a small-system-prompt change.
leah: agreed. next eval will include 4 priming variants + KV warmstart. target: 100k-token synthetic sweep heavy on long-context and rare entities to nail slice CI.
nina: rollback criteria?
omar: runbook bullets:
- monitor: slice_precision (long-sum), user-ctr proxy, p95 latency, decode-error-rate.
- immediate rollback: any slice_precision drop > 2% sustained over 20m OR decode errors > 0.5% absolute.
- soft rollback: overall QA drop > 1% for 60m with p<0.05.
- mitigation steps: throttle int4 traffic, reroute affected tenants to int6, enable prefix caching, increase kv-cache warmstarts.

vik: also add a metric for hallucination-rate (entity hallucination on long-sum) since that's where regression concentrated.
leah: good call.
ops-bot: canary flag created: feature/eng-ml/vanguard-int4-canary (owner: nina).
nina: infra ETA 36h to wire flag+per-route split + dashboard (p95, slice_precision_longsum, fallback_rate, hallucination_rate).
leah: action items:
- vik: run 100k synthetic sweep with priming variants + report (ETA 72h).
- nina: wire canary flag and dashboards (ETA 36h).
- leah: prepare scorecard + TL;DR for GTN + product (ETA 48h).

omar: decision guidance for GTN handoff:
- if int4 overall delta <= -0.5% and long-sum slice recovery > -1% post-priming, approve 25% routing for non-low-latency tenants.
- otherwise restrict to batch-only and keep shadowing.

vik: small note: runtime p95 for int4 is spikier; consider KV cache warmstart and smaller batch sizes for tail-sensitive tenants.
leah: will test warmstart effect in the sweep; also will log decode-error histograms.

nina: ping me when the scorecard lands, we'll schedule a 30-min sync with product if thresholds are borderline.
leah: thanks team. publishing initial findings to the internal repo after the 100k run. :rocket:
thread_text: vanguard 13b int6 vs int4 quickbench, cost-vs-quality discussion, canary + runbook decisions
